hr_010:n4.why: Interviewing candidates and checking references requires live conversation and subjective evaluation of fit and character.

hr_011:n6.why: USCIS requires the signed I-129 package and fee submission to come from an authorized filer taking legal responsibility for its accuracy.

hr_011:n7.why: USCIS adjudication time depends entirely on the agency's internal caseload and processing queue.

ops_013:n1.why: Choosing an MDM vendor is a budget and security-posture tradeoff that only the ops/IT owner can commit to.

ops_013:n4.why: Physically unboxing, imaging, and handing out laptops to distributed employees is hands-on fleet logistics work.

ops_014:n1.why: Sizing headcount and budget for office space depends on internal growth forecasts and financial constraints only leadership can judge.

comp_014:n4.why: A security lead must judge whether draft answers accurately represent the company's actual controls before they become a contractual representation to the customer.

team_001:n2.why: Only the invited teammate can accept the invite email and set their own account credentials.

vc_001:n1.why: Selecting fund formation counsel or a platform is a relationship and cost/quality judgment about who will bear legal responsibility for the fund's documents.

vc_001:n3.why: The Certificate of Limited Partnership must be executed by a general partner attesting to the LP's formation under Delaware law.

vc_001:n3b.why: The step is waiting on the Delaware Division of Corporations to process and return the stamped, file-marked certificate.
vc_001:n3b.computerUseWhy: There is no interface to drive; the fund simply waits for the state's clock to return the stamped document.

vc_001:n5b.why: The GP's signature on the LPA and operating agreement binds the fund to its governing contracts and requires the GP's personal legal authority.
vc_001:n5b.computerUseWhy: Even if routed through an e-sign platform, the GP's execution is a binding contractual act that must be performed by the authorized human, not an agent.

vc_002:n5.why: Holding the first and final close requires the GP to formally certify that closing conditions (subscriptions, funds) have been satisfied.

form_012:n1.why: Deciding whether/when to convert is a strategic judgment call weighing fundraising timeline, cap table dilution, and tax exposure that only the founders can make.

form_012:n4.why: Delaware LLC conversion law requires the actual members (or their authorized signatories) to consent in writing to approve the plan of conversion.
form_012:n4.computerUseWhy: Clicking through an e-sign flow is trivial, but only the members hold the legal authority to bind themselves to the conversion consent.

form_012:n5.why: Delaware requires an officer/authorized person to attest under penalty of law that the Certificate of Conversion and Certificate of Incorporation are accurate before the Division of Corporations will file them.

form_012:n6.why: The company is waiting on the Delaware Division of Corporations to process, stamp, and return the filed certificates on the state's own processing timeline.

form_012:n7.why: Adopting bylaws and authorizing the founder stock issuance are corporate actions that legally require board/incorporator resolution under DGCL, not just document generation.

form_012:n7b.why: Each founder must personally sign their own stock purchase agreement to make a binding, individually-owned equity purchase.
form_012:n7b.computerUseWhy: E-signing is mechanically trivial, but only the individual founder holds the authority to execute their own purchase agreement.

form_012:n8a.why: An IRS 83(b) election requires the taxpayer's own signature attesting under penalty of perjury to the fair market value and election choice.
form_012:n8a.computerUseWhy: Signing a PDF is mechanically simple, but only the individual taxpayer has the legal standing to make this perjury-backed tax election.

form_012:n8.why: The IRS still requires 83(b) elections to be filed by mailing a signed paper form (often certified mail) to the appropriate IRS service center within 30 days, with no e-filing option.
form_012:n8.computerUseWhy: There is no online submission portal for 83(b) elections — the actionUrl is just a static PDF, and actual filing is a physical mailing act, not a web flow.

form_012:n9.why: Converting entity records requires updating bank, payroll (e.g., Gusto/ADP), and state agency accounts to reflect the new C-Corp EIN and entity status across separate third-party systems.
form_012:n9.computerUseWhy: An agent can drive the payroll and state registration web portals to update entity details, but bank entity-conversion changes typically require human-verified identity/authentication steps a bank enforces.
